intro.author: Malachi, a name meaning 'my messenger' (compare 3:1); whether it is a personal name or a title is debated
intro.written: Probably about 460–430 BC, in the Persian period, after the second temple was built
intro.audience: The people and priests of Judah, a small Persian province, generations after the return from exile
intro.setting: The temple had been rebuilt and sacrifices restored, but the excitement of Haggai and Zechariah's day had faded. Priests offered blemished animals, people withheld tithes, men divorced their wives and married outside the faith, and many doubted God cared. Similar problems appear in Nehemiah's time.
intro.purpose: To expose half-hearted worship and broken faithfulness, answer the people's cynical questions, and announce that the Lord himself is coming, preceded by his messenger.
intro.bigIdea: God's covenant love has not changed; his people must return to him and be ready for his coming.
